title: The Failed Payment Spike
description:
**SITUATION:**

Finance saw more card payments fail yesterday than on a normal day. They do not want a dashboard screenshot. The payments lead wants the numbers taken from the raw **payment-handler** log, because that file is what the service actually wrote when each payment was declined.

The log is messy. The same failure is written three ways: `FAILED`, `Failed`, and `failed`. Decline codes look alike: `E402` and `E4021` are different codes, and counting the wrong one will send finance after the wrong batch. Some lines name an order only when the word **declined** is on that line. Config files are spread through several folders under `/etc/payment-handler`, and only some of them set a timeout.

- Log: `/var/log/payment-handler/payments.log`
- Configs: `/etc/payment-handler/` (several folders)

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Extract every line that says **failed**, in any letter case.
2. Count the lines with decline code **`E402`** exactly. `E4021` is a different code.
3. List the unique **order IDs** (`ORD-` followed by 6 digits) that appear on lines with the word **declined**.
4. Find which config files under `/etc/payment-handler` actually **set** a timeout (a line like `read_timeout = 5s`).

**SPEC:**

Every answer goes in `~/answers/` (create it first):

- `failed.txt`: the matching lines, unchanged and in log order
- `e402-count`: just the number of `E402` lines
- `declined-orders`: one order ID per line, no duplicates
- `timeout-configs`: full paths of the configs that set a timeout, one per line

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- Build pipelines step by step. Run each part, look at the output, then add the next `|`.
- `-w` (whole word) and `^` (start of line) remove most false matches.
- Your log is generated per learner. Copying someone else's numbers won't work.

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine with systemd; sudo works without a password.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — The Failed Payment Spike

`grep` prints the lines that match a pattern. A few flags cover most real work:

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `-i` | ignore letter case |
| `-w` | match whole words only (`E402` doesn't match `E4021`) |
| `-c` | count matching lines |
| `-o` | print only the matched part |
| `-E` | extended regex (`{6}`, `+`, `\|`) |
| `-r` / `-l` | search a directory tree / list matching file names |

Docs: `man grep` · `man 7 regex`

```bash
cd /var/log/payment-handler
mkdir -p ~/answers
```

## 1. Every failed payment, in any case

```bash
grep -i 'failed' payments.log > ~/answers/failed.txt
```

## 2. How many E402s

```bash
grep -c 'code=E402' payments.log        # too many: also counts E4021
grep -cw 'code=E402' payments.log > ~/answers/e402-count
```

## 3. Unique order IDs on declined lines

Chain two greps: the first keeps the declined lines, the second cuts out the IDs.

```bash
grep -w 'declined' payments.log | grep -oE 'ORD-[0-9]{6}' | sort -u > ~/answers/declined-orders
```

`-w` skips `predeclined`. `sort -u` sorts and removes duplicates.

## 4. Configs that set a timeout

```bash
grep -ri 'timeout' /etc/payment-handler                # includes a comment line
grep -rlE '^[a-z_]*timeout *=' /etc/payment-handler > ~/answers/timeout-configs
```

`^` anchors the match to the start of the line, so comment lines starting with `#` are skipped.

Then **Submit**.
